"Death Anniversary Rituals"  17-9-2020 Thursday's Message
My Salutations to all Pious Souls....
The period of the 'Shraddha Paksha' is going on; (the period of paying homage to the departed souls - the Hindu scriptures state that the auspicious resolutions and offerings made with reverence for the fulfillment and progress of those who have left their bodies whether they are in any form or in any world is Shraddha) and because of this reason, many sadhaks have messaged me to shed some light on this topic. In the Shraddha Paksha some rituals are performed in memory of one's ancestors. When the soul leaves the body, even after that, various rituals are performed through whose medium the soul is made to feel that it's connection with the physical body has ended - that when your relationship with the body has ended, then your relationship with us too has ended. Now you are free from the body and now you should give up the attachment to this body and to us and proceed on your onward journey. And then by performing the 12th and 13th (day) rituals, that soul is repeatedly reminded that its connection with us has ended. And along with that, we also make ourselves understand that our relationship with it (the departed soul) has ended.
This is a process for coming out of our grief for the departed person. Whenever a near and dear one dies, then you should take a bath and sit down with a calm chitta and meditate and light a lamp for the departed soul's eternal peace. Then 'pray' to your Paramatma (God) for giving eternal 'peace' to that person's soul, and that it attains 'liberation'. After performing such a prayer, you will feel that that soul too has obtained peace along with yourself after the prayer. You did whatever was in your hands for him, and then you too will experience satisfaction and peace.
You too can say such a prayer for your ancestors during the Shraddha Paksha. The 'Shradda Paksha' reminds us that just as our ancestors have left us, similarly we too will definitely have to go one day. This body is perishable, 'the person whose station arrives, that traveller definitely gets off the train'. Our ancestors had been acquiring wealth and property throughout their lives and could not take anything away with them; everything has been left behind here itself. When the Shraddha Paksha awakens such a feeling of emptiness within us, that is when the 'Navratra' of Jagdamba (Goddess) within us arrives, and the ritual of staying awake during Navratri (auspicious period of nine days) takes place.
This time, because of the 'extra month' (Adheek Maas - an extra month in the Hindu calendar that is inserted to keep the lunar and solar calendars aligned) which is being observed, you have got an extra month's time for emptying yourself with your own meditation practice. Make good use of it to prepare yourself for your own 'spiritual progress' during Navratri. Lots of blessings to all of you.
Your own
Baba Swami
17.9.2020
Kutch Samarpan Ashram
Punadi, Kutch (Gujarat)
